        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis.

            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run recipe** that will:

1. Clone the repo  
2. Inspect its contents (the repo is a tiny Node.js “Hello World” app)  
3. Generate a Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAMLs and a GitHub Actions workflow  
4. Commit the new files and push them back to the repo

> **NOTE** – The script assumes you already have an SSH key added to your GitHub account and that you have permission to push to the `main` branch.  
> If you’re using HTTPS instead of SSH, replace the clone URL accordingly.

---

## 1. Clone the repository

```bash
# 1.1 Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2. Analyse the repo & create artefacts

### 2.1 Dockerfile

The repo contains a very small Node.js app (`app.js`) that listens on port **3000**.  
A minimal Dockerfile for this app looks like:

```Dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# 1️⃣  Base image
FROM node:18-alpine

# 2️⃣  Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# 3️⃣  Copy package files & install deps
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# 4️⃣  Copy source code
COPY . .

# 5️⃣  Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# 6️⃣  Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why node:18‑alpine?**  
> Alpine images are tiny, and Node 18 is the LTS version at the time of writing.  
> Feel free to bump the Node version if you need newer features.

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAMLs

We’ll create a **Deployment** and a **Service** that expose the app inside a cluster.

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
# k8s/service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **Where to put the YAMLs?**  
> Create a `k8s/` directory at the repo root and drop the two files there.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

The workflow will:

1. Checkout the repo  
2. Log in to Docker Hub (or any registry you prefer)  
3. Build the Docker image  
4. Push the image to the registry  
5. (Optional) Deploy to a Kubernetes cluster – you can add that later

Create `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # 1️⃣ Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # 2️⃣ Set up Docker Buildx
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # 3️⃣ Log in to Docker Hub
      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      # 4️⃣ Build and push the image
      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **Secrets**  
> Add `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` to the repo’s *Settings → Secrets → Actions*.

---

## 3. Add, commit and push the new files

```bash
# 3.1 Create directories & files
mkdir -p k8s
cat <<'EOF' > Dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /usr/src/app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: \${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: \${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
EOF

# 3.2 Stage the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml

# 3.3 Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests and CI workflow"

# 3.4 Push to main
git push origin main
```

---

## 4. Verify

1. **GitHub Actions** – After the push, the *Actions* tab should show a successful run.  
2. **Docker Hub** – You should see the `zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest` image.  
3. **Kubernetes** – Apply the manifests:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/
```

You can then expose the service via `kubectl port-forward svc/nodejs-welcome-service 8080:80` and visit `http://localhost:8080`.

---

### Recap of the artefacts created

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight image for the Node.js app |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas of the app |
| `k8s/service.yaml` | Exposes the app inside the cluster |
| `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image |

Feel free to tweak the Docker image tag, registry, or Kubernetes settings to match your environment. Happy coding!
